title: Customer governance request signal-hub, priority pipeline, and action matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit heterogeneous governance requests (logging redaction, retention changes, PII export/removal, audit exports). Current intake is inconsistent: requests lack standard signals, routing is ad-hoc, and prioritization relies on tribal knowledge. This work creates a "signal hub" that standardizes incoming governance requests into a scored priority pipeline and a prescriptive action matrix that maps priority -> triage owner, SLA, default remediation steps, and escalation paths. Scope: non-bug customer requests relating to data governance controls (redaction, retention, PII handling, audit exports). Out of scope: legal subpoenas, internal security incidents, and infra-only outages. Goals: 1) Reduce manual classification time by 60% for enterprise requests; 2) Surface a single canonical priority score for routing to Support/Customer Success/Legal/Security; 3) Provide runbook actions for the top 10 request archetypes so first-touch resolution improves by 40%; 4) Ensure every routed ticket includes explicit data classification, affected products, and recommended SLA tier.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical request intake form (web + API) with a minimal set of required signals: customer_tier, data_type, request_type (redaction|retention|pii|audit_export), retention_window_change, urgency_reason, sample_logs_or_policy_link.
An automated scoring function implemented in the intake pipeline that emits a single priority label (P0_high|P1_medium|P2_low) and numeric score, stored on the Linear ticket as metadata.

A 3x3 action matrix mapping (priority x request archetype) -> recommended first-touch action, owner group, and default SLA. Action matrix published in Confluence and surfaced as a link in the Linear ticket template.

Default routing rules implemented: P0 -> Pager/Security oncall + PM alert; P1 -> Customer Success + Solutions Engineering; P2 -> Product backlog or scheduled intake. Routing verified in two staged tests with synthetic requests.

Telemetry: dashboard showing intake volume by archetype, mean time to first action by priority, and percent of tickets resolved using recommended actions. Dashboard populated and visible to PM/Support/Legal groups.

Runbook for top-10 archetypes with template email snippets, required audit evidence checklist, and a safe-fallback policy for unsupported requests. Runbook reviewed and signed off by Legal and Security.
Documentation and an internal launch email to CS/Support/Legal with training notes and escalation contact list.
Security review completed and KMS or data handling constraints documented for any automated exports.
steps: Workshop with Support, CS, Legal, Security to enumerate request archetypes (complete, 2025-01-14).
Draft intake schema and minimal signals; iterate with Solutions Eng for feasibility (draft v1 on Confluence).
Implement intake form in Support portal and ingestion webhook to Linear via middleware service (engineering spike to estimate).
Build scoring function: rule-based prototype for initial launch, telemetry hooks for model-based scoring evaluation later.
Design and publish action matrix in Confluence; collect sign-offs from stakeholders.
Create Linear ticket template that auto-populates score and required evidence links.
Instrument dashboard (Looker/Metabase) with KPIs and verify data freshness and accuracy.
Pilot with three customers and two CS reps for 2 weeks; collect feedback and iterate.
Launch internal training, update runbooks, and deprecate legacy intake spreadsheets.
Post-launch 30/60-day review to decide on scoring model upgrade and automation opportunities.
If pilot meets success criteria, schedule roadmap work for ML-assisted triage in Q3 2025.
Link follow-ups to release planning (console-2025.03) and Dedicated onboarding flows where relevant.

decision_history: 2025-01-14 Decision: Use a hybrid priority model (rule-based scoring for launch; collect features for later ML model). Rationale: faster time-to-value and auditability.
2025-01-20 Decision: Minimum intake signals chosen to balance engineer effort and operator data needs (customer_tier, request_type, data_type, urgency_reason, sample_link).
2025-01-27 Decision: Action matrix will default to a human owner group (Support/CS/Legal/Security) rather than full automation for P0 due to high risk.
2025-02-03 Decision: Priority labels will be stored as a Linear custom field and mirrored to Support portal for routing.
2025-02-10 Decision: Audit export requests require explicit Legal signoff in the runbook; any automated exports must pass KMS data-handling checklist.
2025-02-12 Decision: Pilot must include telemetry proving 40% improvement in first-touch resolution or work will be paused for redesign.
notes: Tradeoffs discussed: strict mandatory fields improve routing accuracy but reduce customer friction — we agreed on progressive profiling where portal asks minimally first then requests evidence on escalation.
Fallback policy: If required evidence is missing for P0/P1, ticket auto-escalates to human triage and customer is prompted for evidence with templated email.
Edge-case: PII deletion requests for on-prem Dedicated customers may require manual coordination with the customer's infra team; add as special-case to action matrix.
Monitoring: Add an alert if >10% of tickets are re-classified from P2->P0 within 24 hours (indicator of scoring gaps).
Privacy: Ensure intake form does not accept raw PII payloads (use links or hashed identifiers); Security to validate payload handling before GA.
Internationalization: Retention law differences noted for EU customers — introduce a jurisdiction signal in the next iteration.
Follow-ups: Link to onboarding flow for Dedicated customers so CS can pre-populate retention policy references during intake.
Metrics target: MTTA (mean time to acknowledge) for P0 targets < 1 hour, P1 < 24 hours, P2 < 7 days for initial triage.
Risks: Automated exports have the highest risk — require Legal + Security signoff and audit trail before enabling automation.
Success criteria for pilot: >= 60% reduction in manual downstream classification, >= 40% improvement in first-touch resolution for archetype-supported tickets.
